summary: A Civilian Conservation Corps lookout on Palomar Mountain's high point gave way to a 67-ft steel tower in 1964; volunteers have staffed it since 2009.

facts.design: 13x13-ft CL-30 steel cab on a 67-ft all-steel L-1600 tower

access.note: A hiking write-up dated April 2024 (not an agency source) says the public is prohibited from ascending the tower. The summit is reachable on foot.

visit.trail_note: A hiking write-up describes a walk along a dirt road to the summit; a gate blocks vehicles for the last stretch.

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Cleveland National Forest

events.note: First lookout on the site, built by the Civilian Conservation Corps. The register describes a 45-ft tower with a ground cabin.
Current structure built at Palomar Mountain on the Cleveland National Forest.
The current 67-ft steel tower and cab replaced the 1935 structure.
The Cleveland National Forest last staffed the tower.
Interior removed due to vandalism; a security gate was installed on the tower.
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register on June 2, 2008.
Restoration with new glass, cabinets and flooring completed.
San Diego-Riverside chapter of the FFLA began staffing the tower with volunteers.
Chapter first achieved 100% fire-season staffing; it has continued with few exceptions since.
Repair of a problematic solar and propane incinerating outhouse at the site.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives the current cab as 14 by 14 feet; the chapter gives 13 by 13 feet. The record uses the chapter's figure.
The first lookout on the site dates to 1935 (CCC). The current tower dates to 1964. The record's 1964 is the current structure, and the 1935 first lookout is added to events.
The register and chapter say volunteers staff the tower daily in fire season; a hiking write-up says the public may not ascend it. Treated as restricted, with climbing not offered.

sources.title: Hiking to the high point of Palomar Mountain

notes_for_editor: The record's 2009 note that the lookout was staffed 81 of 171 possible days could not be found in the pages read, so it is not used. The record's 2017 'restored' event is an outhouse repair; it is kept here as 'other'. The 1935 first lookout is missing from the record and is added. The cab size differs between the register (14 by 14 ft) and the chapter (13 by 13 ft). The public-access note rests on a hiking blog, not an agency page; confirm it with the Palomar Ranger District before publishing. Staffing as_of is the chapter's 'every year since 2013' claim, not a dated census.
